description.headline: Going from 4 KB to 2 MB pages cuts latency by 86% for multi-level and 61% for single-level.
points: Larger pages need fewer translations, so the TLB misses less and each access gets faster.
At 4 KB, single-level is best (2.6 cycles) and multi-level is worst (7.3 cycles), a 2.8x gap.
The ranking of the page-table types is the same at every point.
At 2 MB the working set fits in the TLB, so almost every access hits it and the table type stops mattering.
description.held: sequential access, 64-entry TLB, 1 process, medium memory, 100,000 accesses

description.headline: From small to large memory, single-level grows 256x (2.00 MiB to 512.00 MiB) while multi-level grows only 1.6x (44 KiB to 72 KiB).
